narrative_purpose: Show buoyancy control as a one-way budget withdrawal: water ballast dumps from the animal and the whole caravan rises.
subject: A fifty-metre translucent Medusoid bell seen from the side above a dark mountain ridge. A bright clear column of water is being released from a muscular vent low in the body, falling in a long sparkling stream toward the valley. Several woven gondolas hang beneath the bell, and their position is visibly higher than the level of the distant ridge. Tiny blue-skinned crew figures work around the vent and water tanks.
scene: Open Pandoran sky above layered mountain ridges and cloud, the water stream the one strong vertical element in the frame.
camera: Three-quarter side view at the level of the gondolas, enough distance to see the entire bell and the falling ballast.
light: Cool twilight haze, the released water catches pale cyan light; a single small amber cooking fire glows in one gondola.
palette: Deep indigo sky and mountain, translucent cyan bell, bright pale water stream, one tiny ember amber accent.
style: Painterly speculative-biology naturalist plate, observed and quiet.
detail_level: Crisp on the vent, water stream and gondola harness; distant ridge dissolves into haze.
composition: Bell in the upper half, water stream descending near one side, gondolas beneath, generous plain dark sky for later callout labels.
consistency_notes: The animal rises because water is being dumped, not because of a visible engine or wingbeat. Keep the ballast stream visually unmistakable and the bell consistent with fig-00-cover.
negative_prompt: no text, no lettering, no numbers, no labels, no propellers, no metal airship, no explosion, no 3D-render or photographic look, no cartoon style
